transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) http5xx FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Frontend and search are much slower in the incident window, while the other services look roughly normal. Next I'll break latency down by span name and span kind to see which calls are slow.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(max(duration)/1e6,2) max_ms, string_agg(DISTINCT attr_status_code, ',') st, string_agg(DISTINCT CAST(attr_http_response_status_code AS VARCHAR), ',') codes FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(max(duration)/1e6,2), string_agg(DISTINCT attr_status_code, ','), string_agg(DISTINCT CAST(attr_http_response_status_code AS VARCHAR), ',') FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The slowdown sits on the `search → geo.Geo/Nearby` client span (about 1.5 s), while geo's own server span stays at about 0.15 ms. The delay is therefore between search and geo, not inside geo. Next I'll check the network metrics on that connection and the metric names available.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(max(value),2) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 2,3,4,5,1

SELECT 'abn_sum' src, metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm_sum', metric, count(*), count(DISTINCT service_name) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'abn_g', metric, count(*), count(DISTINCT service_name) FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm_g', metric, count(*), count(DISTINCT service_name) FROM normal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: No hubble network metrics exist in this case. Next I'll check whether the search or geo pods show restarts, uptime resets, or resource pressure, and what the logs say.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) FROM normal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,4,1

SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, count(*) n, round(min(value),1) mn, round(max(value),1) mx FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='k8s.pod.uptime' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, metric, count(*), round(min(value),1), round(max(value),1) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric='k8s.pod.uptime' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: The logs contain no errors, only INFO messages. The client span on search→geo takes about 1.5 s while the geo server span takes 0.15 ms, so the time is spent before geo handles the request. Next I'll check CPU and memory on search and geo to rule out resource exhaustion on either side.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, metric, round(avg(value),3) avg_v, round(max(value),3) max_v, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','geo','frontend') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.working_set','container.cpu.usage') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, metric, round(avg(value),3), round(max(value),3), count(*) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','geo','frontend') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.working_set','container.cpu.usage') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: CPU and memory are flat on search, geo and frontend, so there is no resource saturation. Next I'll check whether the extra time comes before the geo server span starts, which would confirm on-wire delay.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, count(*) n, round(avg(epoch_ms(s.time) - epoch_ms(c.time)),1) start_gap_ms, round(avg((epoch_ms(c.time)+c.duration/1e6) - (epoch_ms(s.time)+s.duration/1e6)),1) end_gap_ms FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='geo.Geo/Nearby' UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', count(*), round(avg(epoch_ms(s.time) - epoch_ms(c.time)),1), round(avg((epoch_ms(c.time)+c.duration/1e6) - (epoch_ms(s.time)+s.duration/1e6)),1) FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='geo.Geo/Nearby'

content.text: The gap is about 1,529 ms before the geo server span starts and about 5 ms on the return, so the delay is on the request leg before geo handles it. To tell a network fault from an application-level hold at search, I'll check the pod network counters for search and geo.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, count(*) n, round(avg(value),1) avg_v, round(max(value),1) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE service_name IN ('search','geo','frontend','rate') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.errors','k8s.pod.network.io') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), round(avg(value),1), round(max(value),1) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE service_name IN ('search','geo','frontend','rate') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.network.errors','k8s.pod.network.io') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 3,2,1
